title: Preservation Across a True Register Equality Test
statement: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register machine with oracle, input $x$, and configuration guard $G$. Suppose the instruction at live state $l$ tests whether registers $r$ and $s$ are equal, continuing at $l_1$ if they are equal and at $l_0$ otherwise. If the configuration with state $l$, valuation $v$, and no answer satisfies $G$, the two register values are equal, and the configuration at state $l_1$ with valuation $v$ and no answer is terminating under $G$ and accepts exactly when proposition $P$ holds, then the original configuration has those same properties.
hypotheses_covered: The instruction at state l tests equality of registers r and s, with branches l1 and l0
The values v(r) and v(s) are equal
The l1 successor is terminating under G and accepts exactly when P holds
